decision: Bound the occupancy lease with an absolute 8-hour age cap on claimed_at that no refresh path may extend

governingRule.description: Occupancy is a bearer-string boundary, so lease liveness must stay bounded by something a holder cannot extend, or the heartbeat TTL stops reclaiming worktrees from dead sessions

alternativesConsidered.option: Heartbeat TTL only, refreshed by the owner's writes (no absolute bound)
A shorter cap near a single long session, such as four hours
Bound liveness by a liveness probe of the holder's process instead of by clock

whyWinner: Refresh without a bound lets any process holding the occupant's session id keep a worktree forever, which disables the crash-recovery reclaim the TTL exists for. Keying the cap on claimed_at and deciding it where liveness is decided makes it unreachable from every refresh path. Eight hours (24 TTLs) is a wide multiple of the longest legitimate sessions observed here while bounding reclaim to one working day; a shorter cap would interrupt real sessions, a 24-hour cap would not reclaim the same day, and process probing is out of the cooperative local-file model. Reaching the cap costs one re-claim, not the work.
revisitTrigger: Revisit if legitimate sessions routinely exceed eight hours, if operators report re-claim churn at the bound, or if occupancy gains an authenticated holder identity that makes bearer-string reasoning obsolete
